quality_attributes.name: Security and privacy
quality_attributes.description: The system must protect user identity data, authentication factors, biometric information, and payment-related information from unauthorized access or disclosure.
quality_attributes.rationale: The requirements explicitly call for encryption of user information, biometric login handling, and secure payment processing, and the project description requires compliance with GDPR, the Privacy Directive, and ISO 27001.
evidence: S1 requires user information to be secured with end-to-end encryption.
S3 requires login via email/password or biometric thumb-impression and states the thumb impression must be flushed out after login.
S8 requires payment via bank account or debit/credit card.
Project description requires GDPR, Privacy Directive, and ISO 27001 compliance.

quality_attributes.name: Usability
quality_attributes.description: The system must be easy to understand and operate for riders on both web and mobile devices.
quality_attributes.rationale: The project description explicitly states that the software should be user-friendly and easy to use for all potential riders, and several functional requirements involve user-facing flows such as registration, login, nearby bike discovery, navigation, payment, and history access.
evidence: Project description states the software should be user-friendly and easy to use for all potential riders.
S1-S3 describe registration and login interactions.
S5-S6 describe locating and registering a bike.
S8 describes payment selection.
S11 describes access to usage history.

quality_attributes.name: Availability
quality_attributes.description: The service must remain accessible when riders need to register, locate bikes, rent bikes, and complete payments through both web and mobile access.
quality_attributes.rationale: The system is intended for operational use by riders and administrators, and the project description emphasizes access through both web and mobile devices to maximize service availability.
evidence: Project description states the software should be accessible through both web and mobile devices to maximize availability of the service.
S5-S6 depend on users being able to access available bikes and register them.
S8 requires payment processing.
S12 requires administrator visibility of bikes.

quality_attributes.name: Performance and responsiveness
quality_attributes.description: The system should respond quickly enough to support time-sensitive actions such as verification code handling, location-based bike discovery, bike registration, session timeout enforcement, and expiry notifications.
quality_attributes.rationale: Several requirements impose explicit or implicit time constraints, and location-based and rental-time flows depend on timely system response.
evidence: S2 defines verification-code timing constraints.
S4 defines a 15-minute inactivity logout.
S5 involves finding nearby bikes within a proximity threshold.
S6 and S7 require timely bike selection and availability updates.
S9 requires notification before rental expiry.
S10 defines rental duration limits.

quality_attributes.name: Data consistency
quality_attributes.description: Bike availability, rental state, usage history, and administrative status views must remain consistent as users rent bikes and administrators inspect operational data.
quality_attributes.rationale: The functional requirements depend on accurate updates to bike availability and reporting data, and inconsistencies would directly affect rentals and reporting accuracy.
evidence: S7 requires a bike to be removed from availability after registration.
S11 requires history for the last 3 months.
S12 requires viewing bikes as available or under utilization.
S13 requires hourly and daily usage statistics.

quality_attributes.name: Interoperability
quality_attributes.description: The system must work with external communication and payment services and operate across web and mobile client channels.
quality_attributes.rationale: The project description requires compatibility with third-party payment platforms and access through web and mobile devices, which implies the system must exchange data with external services and support multiple client types.
evidence: Project description requires compatibility with a variety of third-party payment platforms.
S2 allows verification by SMS or email.
S8 requires payment via bank account or debit/credit card.

quality_attributes.name: Localization and regulatory compliance
quality_attributes.description: The system must comply with applicable regional regulations and standards depending on deployment location.
quality_attributes.rationale: The project description explicitly requires compliance with EU or China standards depending on the university location, in addition to GDPR, the Privacy Directive, and ISO 27001.
evidence: Project description requires GDPR and Privacy Directive compliance.
Project description requires ISO 27001 compliance.
Project description requires compliance with local regulations and standards, including EU or China standards, depending on location.

quality_attributes.name: Scalability
quality_attributes.description: The system should be able to handle growth in riders, bikes, and administrative reporting demand without degrading core service behavior.
quality_attributes.rationale: The project description targets city-wide bike sharing with location discovery and multi-channel access, and the functional requirements include rider and administrator operations that may need to scale with usage volume.
evidence: Project description describes a city bike service for riders in and around the city.
S5 requires location-based listing of available bikes.
S12 and S13 require city-wide administrative views and usage reporting.
